headline: Black Friday is the last very warm day, with highs in the 80s around 15 degrees above normal in the Los Angeles valleys, before a cooler, showery Sunday and Monday lead into a near-certain moderate to strong storm Monday night through early Wednesday with 1 to 3 inches of rain in the coasts and valleys, 3 to 5 inches in the foothills, possible thunderstorms and strong winds.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Friday stays sunny, very warm and dry, with highs in the low to mid 80s across the coasts and valleys of Los Angeles and Ventura counties, including the Glendale area, about 15 degrees above normal, and mid to upper 70s in San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties. Records are mostly out of reach, but a few spots could come within a couple of degrees. The dry northeast Santa Ana winds are fading, with only lingering gusts in a few areas, and skies stay mostly clear tonight.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday stays dry and mostly clear as winds turn onshore (from the ocean) in the afternoon, cooling most areas 3 to 6 degrees, though highs still end up 3 to 6 degrees above normal. Sunday turns mostly cloudy and another 4 to 8 degrees cooler, bringing highs back to normal. A weak disturbance brings a chance of light rain to the Central Coast Sunday afternoon, rain is likely there (70 percent) Sunday evening, and there's a 30 to 40 percent chance of light rain south of Point Conception, including Los Angeles County. Areas north of Morro Bay may see a quarter inch, but everywhere else gets at most a tenth of an inch and likely much less.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Monday brings on-and-off rain ahead of the main storm, with a quarter to a third of an inch for the coasts, valleys and coastal mountain slopes, much less in the far interior, and highs dropping into the mid 60s to lower 70s. Forecasters put the chance of a moderate to strong storm Monday night through early Wednesday near 100 percent: a cold low pressure system passing overhead, unusually high moisture and warm ocean temperatures raise the odds of thunderstorms, with 1 to 3 inches of rain for the coasts and valleys and 3 to 5 inches for the coastal slopes and foothills. There's also a greater than normal chance of strong winds with gusts over 50 mph; the storm is pulling in warm subtropical moisture, so snow levels stay at or above 7,500 feet, and highs are in the mid 60s Tuesday and Wednesday. Thursday looks dry, with a weak, likely minor system Friday.

coast: A large, long-period west swell slowly eases. Exceptionally high tides of 7.4 to 7.7 feet Friday morning bring a threat of moderate coastal flooding to low-lying spots, with high surf, on the Central Coast from Point Conception northward and on the Ventura and Los Angeles County coasts, and minor flooding possible elsewhere; tides up to 7.2 feet Saturday morning keep moderate flooding going on the Ventura County coast around the late-morning high tide. Coastal Flood Advisories run until 4 PM Friday for many beaches and until 2 PM Saturday for the Ventura County beaches, High Surf Advisories run until 3 PM or 9 PM Saturday depending on the stretch of coast, and a Beach Hazards Statement covers other beaches through Saturday afternoon. Expect many strong rip currents nearly everywhere, strong along-shore currents, some risk of sneaker waves, heavy shore break and coastal erosion, making swimming dangerous. On the water, a Small Craft Advisory runs until 3 AM Saturday for rough seas on the outer waters and north of Point Sal; conditions are mostly calmer Saturday through Monday, then winds rise to advisory levels Monday evening and to gale force late Monday night through Tuesday night, with large, increasingly hazardous seas as the strong storm arrives.
watch_for: Timing and details of the Monday night–early Wednesday storm, including heavy rain and possible thunderstorms
Strong winds with gusts over 50 mph during that storm
Coastal flooding at Saturday morning's high tide on the Ventura County coast
confidence: Confidence is high in warm, dry weather through Saturday and near 100 percent that a moderate to strong storm arrives Monday night into early Wednesday, though forecasters say it's still too early to pin down its finer details and timing.
